title: Flat coefficientwise power-series extension and its local faithfully flat form
statement:
Let $A,B$ be commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\rho:A\to B$ be a flat ring homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and let $n\ge0$. Put $R=A[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]$, $T=B[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The coefficientwise homomorphism
$$\rho_*:R\longrightarrow T,\qquad \sum_\alpha a_\alpha Z^\alpha\longmapsto\sum_\alpha\rho(a_\alpha)Z^\alpha$$
is flat. If $B$ is nonzero local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$, put $\mathfrak n=(\mathfrak m_B,Z)T$ and $\mathfrak q=\rho_*^{-1}(\mathfrak n)$. Then the induced local homomorphism $R_{\mathfrak q}\to T$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. For $n=0$ these assertions concern $\rho$ itself and its indicated localization.

source.place: Tag 0523 (lemma-flat-module-powers), applied to the ideal of formal variables; agent coefficientwise specialization and local corollary. The complete argument is retained in the worker report, not asserted to be the verbatim statement of this tag.

proof.text: Put $I=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)R$ and $J=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)T=IT$. For each $k\ge1$, a series lies in $I^k$ exactly when all coefficients of total degree less than $k$ vanish: one direction follows by multiplication, and for the converse assign each monomial of degree at least $k$ to a chosen degree-$k$ divisor and group the terms into the finitely many resulting multiples. The same argument holds over $B$. Thus $R/I^k$ and $T/J^k$ have unique representatives $\sum_{|\alpha|<k}a_\alpha Z^\alpha$ and $\sum_{|\alpha|<k}b_\alpha Z^\alpha$, with multiplication given by convolution discarding degrees at least $k$.

proof.text: Write $C_k=R/I^k$. The finite monomial bases in Step 1 identify $C_k\otimes_A B$ with $T/J^k$ by $[aZ^\alpha]\otimes b\mapsto\rho(a)bZ^\alpha$; the convolution formula proves multiplicativity and identifies the map from $C_k$ with the quotient of $\rho_*$. This map is flat directly from the definition: for an injection $N\hookrightarrow N\prime$ of $C_k$-modules, the identifications $N\otimes_{C_k}(C_k\otimes_A B)\simeq N\otimes_A B$, $x\otimes(c\otimes b)\mapsto cx\otimes b$, inverse $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes(1\otimes b)$, and likewise for $N\prime$, turn the induced map into tensoring the underlying $A$-module injection with the flat $A$-module $B$. Hence $T/J^k$ is flat over $R/I^k$ for every $k\ge1$.

proof.text: Every maximal ideal $Q$ of $T$ contains $J$. Indeed, for $h\in J$ and $t\in T$, the formal sum $\sum_{r\ge0}(th)^r$ is well-defined coefficient by coefficient (the $r$th summand has degree at least $r$) and multiplication gives $(1-th)\sum_{r\ge0}(th)^r=1$. If $h\notin Q$, its nonzero image in the field $T/Q$ has an inverse represented by some $t$, forcing the unit $1-th$ into $Q$, a contradiction. For $n=0$ the ideal is zero and the assertion is immediate.

proof.text: The power-series Noetherianity node applied to $A$ and $B$ makes $R$ and $T$ Noetherian. Apply the flat-module-powers node with ring map $\rho_*:R\to T$, ideal $I$, and finite $T$-module $M=T$ (generated by $1$). Its quotient-flatness hypothesis is precisely Step 2, since $I^kT=J^k$. By Step 3 every maximal ideal $Q$ of $T$ contains $IT$, so this node gives $T_Q$ flat over $R$ for every maximal $Q$. The maximal-localization flatness criterion, with base $R$, algebra $T$, and module $T$, now gives $T$ flat over $R$. It also covers the zero ring $T$, where there are no maximal ideals.

source.place: Agent finite-monomial and geometric-series calculations assembling lemma-flat-module-powers (Tag 0523), lemma-Noetherian-power-series (Tag 0306), lemma-flat-localization (Tag 00HT), and lemma-local-flat-ff (Tag 00HR).

proof.text: Assume now that $B$ is nonzero local. The power-series local-ring node says that $T$ is local with maximal ideal the series whose constant coefficient lies in $\mathfrak m_B$. This ideal equals $\mathfrak n=(\mathfrak m_B,Z)T$: subtracting the constant term leaves a series in $J$ by Step 1 with $k=1$. Hence $\mathfrak q=\rho_*^{-1}(\mathfrak n)$ is prime. Apply the flat-local-ring-maps node to the flat map of Step 4 at $\mathfrak n$. It gives a flat local map $R_{\mathfrak q}\to T_{\mathfrak n}$. Every element outside $\mathfrak n$ is already a unit in $T$, so $T_{\mathfrak n}\simeq T$ by $t/s\mapsto ts^{-1}$, with inverse $t\mapsto t/1$. The resulting map $R_{\mathfrak q}\to T$ is flat and local. The flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat node therefore makes it faithfully flat. When $n=0$, Step 1 identifies $R=A$, $T=B$ and $\rho_*=\rho$, yielding exactly the stated zero-variable assertions.
